children: , the integrated energy and LNG giant, climbed approximately 1.8% to $93.07 Tuesday as Brent crude jumped more than 2% to around $92.66 a barrel. The catalyst was clear. Renewed Middle East fighting pushed supply fearsand oil's geopolitical premiumstraight back into the market.

Then came the portfolio angle. Shell is reportedly considering offers for U.S. chemical assets worth as much as $8 billion. A Reuters Breakingviews analysis estimated that the company invested roughly $25 billion across chemicals, including $14 billion in Pennsylvania's Monaca complex. The payoff has been ugly. The division generated a negative 2% return on invested capital in 2024.

An $8 billion sale would recover just 32% of that historical investment. That is a painful haircutbut potentially a smart exit from a chronically weak business. Shell's latest quarter delivered $21.4 billion in operating cash flow and $17.5 billion in free cash flow, giving management room to reject a bad price. The valuation snapshot adds one warning: the $93.07 share price stands 11.34% above its $83.59 GF Value estimate. Higher oil brings the cash. A chemicals exit could bring a cleaner story.

title: Shell Rallies as Oil Jumps, Weighs $8 Billion Chemicals Sale
